column1: # Depth ledger — the answer to "what evidence supports this file's coverage?"
# `status` says what a phase was SUPPOSED to do with a file. `depth` says what the evidence actually
# supports. Before this file, `depth` could only be carried forward from the previous manifest, so
# there was no way to ASSERT a depth for a set of files — and no way to state a REASON. That is what
# produced the contradiction Path A Step 4 exists to fix: 1,723 rows reading `status=read` next to
# `depth=sweep-only`, one column claiming the file was read and the other denying it.
# The four depth values, and what each one is allowed to mean:
#   evidenced   Some note in the knowledge graph cites this file. The strongest claim. NOT set here —
#               it is maintained in the manifest itself and carried across regeneration, because it
#               follows the KG's citations rather than a path pattern.
#   agent-read  A named report says an agent read this file in full. The report must exist in `_inbox/`.
#   parsed      A deterministic parser processed this file and the ledger NAMES the parser and what it
#               extracted. This is the value Step 3 adds. It is not weaker than `agent-read` — for
#               generated files it is stronger, because it is reproducible.
#   sweep-only  Covered by a bulk grep/pattern pass, with a stated reason below. An honest gap.
# FORMAT: <js-regex>  TAB  <depth>  TAB  <evidence — parser named, or report named, or reason>
# First match wins. Order matters. Blank lines and `#` comments ignored.
# Excluded files never reach here; they are `n/a` by construction.
# parsed — deterministic extraction, parser named (Path A Step 3)
